illustrative_assumptions: Synthetic broad U.S. equity index at 7,750 on the illustrative issue date (6 October 2026). The level is in the neighbourhood of the documented S&P 500 prints of ~7,700-7,750 on 15-16 October but the index is synthetic.

Pre-shock market: 1y ATM implied volatility 19% (the documented VIX, a 30-day measure, was 16-18); zero curve 4.75% + 0.70% x (1 - exp(-t/5)), anchoring the 10y near the documented 5.36% peak (2y 4.98%, 10y 5.36%); dividend yield 1.2%.

Illustrative shock applied instantaneously to the block: equity -12% (the documented seven-session semiconductor-index drawdown applied to the broad index as an escalation scenario; the documented broad-market drawdown was roughly 2-4%), ATM implied volatility +8 points to 27% (the documented VIX move was about +2 points), parallel zero-curve shift -25 bp (inside the documented 5.36% -> 5.07%-5.19% move).

Synthetic $500M block of newly issued RILA, FIA, and IUL segments struck at 7,750, backed by a Treasury strip ladder whose market value equalled the liability PV at issue. The index-linked credits are not yet hedged at the valuation date; the case study is the hedge-design decision at the stressed market.

Forward-looking scenario distribution for hedge design and evaluation (roughly a one-month horizon in the stressed regime): Student-t(4) index shocks with 7.8% standard deviation, implied-volatility shocks of -0.30 x index return plus N(0, 2.5 pts) noise (clipped to [-15, +40] points), and independent N(0, 35 bp) parallel rate shocks. In-sample and out-of-sample sets use different seeds.

Hedge budget 0.75% of account value ($3.75M) of gross option premium (premium received on sold options is counted as consumed, the engine's conservative convention); liquidity budget $10M of cash for initial margin and premium (equity futures 10% of notional, Treasury futures 2.5% of face, options at premium); position caps per instrument; transaction costs (futures $15, Treasury futures $25, options 1.5% of premium per contract).

limitations: Model-consistent test: hedges are designed and evaluated with the same engine (Black-Scholes replication, GBM Monte Carlo without skew for FIA/IUL). Out-of-sample means different scenario draws, not a different model; basis, skew dynamics, and jump risk are not represented.
Shocks are instantaneous; one-month carry is reported separately. Rebalancing between shocks, margin calls over time, and path-dependent gap risk are not simulated.

FIA and IUL values use 3,000 antithetic paths with common random numbers, so scenario differences are smooth but absolute PVs carry Monte Carlo error of roughly 0.05%; their finite-difference gamma is statistically noise (see the validation report).

One-day finite-difference theta on the 20-year IUL is dominated by a monthly time-grid re-discretization artefact in the engine; carry is therefore measured with a one-month step and theta is not used in the hedge design.
The premium budget counts gross option premium (sold options consume budget), which penalizes the natural short-put-spread RILA hedge; margin on short options is approximated by premium.

Treasury exposure is a zero-coupon proxy valued off the engine's risk-free curve; futures basis, repo, cheapest-to-deliver, and credit spreads on the backing assets are ignored. Behaviour (lapse, mortality) is applied only to IUL, and RILA/FIA are valued to maturity without decrements.

Scenario correlations (vol beta -0.30 to the index, rates independent) are assumptions. The documented October 2026 pattern mixed yields-up/equities-down (CPI day) and yields-down/equities-down (flight to quality) sessions.
Hedge-effectiveness figures are variance and ES95 reductions over the stated shock distribution; they are not regulatory, accounting, or realized effectiveness measures.
notice: Illustrative research exercise. The simulated shocks, the synthetic $500M portfolio, the backing assets, the hedge instruments, and every model-generated hedge are assumptions, not Pacific Life positions, hedges, or trading decisions. Documented market events are listed separately with their sources.

20y indexed account: 11% annual cap, 100% participation, 0% floor, 1.25% charge, 3.5% lapse, 0.3% mortality

recommendation.label: Stress-aware constrained (scenario P&L + CVaR)
rationale: Out-of-sample variance reduction 93.7% (best among the three is 93.7%); dollar-offset slope 0.85; ES95 reduction 73.0%.
Decision rule: highest out-of-sample variance reduction, with strategies within two points treated as equivalent and the tie broken by lower cost, then by ES95 reduction.

Robustness: with positions fixed, variance reduction ranges from 88.0% (No vol-spot correlation) to 96.3% (Inflation-scare rates) across 4 alternative shock distributions; the chosen strategy ranks first in 4 of 4.
